docs.title: Douki
docs.text:
YAML docstrings with types supplied by annotations.

Write descriptions in your docstrings and types in Python annotations. Douki enriches documentation when you inspect it, while its CLI validates and formats the YAML in your source files.

def add(a: int, b: int = 0) -> int:
    """
    title: Add two integers.
    parameters:
      a: First value.
      b: Second value.
    returns: Sum of a and b.
    """
    return a + b

docs.title: Inspect documentation
docs.text:
Register the library once in its __init__.py:

# mylib/__init__.py
import douki

douki.register(__name__)

Users then call ordinary Python help:

import mylib

help(mylib.add)  # Douki descriptions enriched with annotation types
help(len)        # Regular Python help

Registration covers the package and its submodules, including future imports. Objects defined in other libraries retain regular help, even when re-exported by your package. No per-function decorators or user activation calls are needed. The shared help wrapper routes by defining package; importing Douki alone does not install it. Original __doc__ strings remain authored text.

Tools can call douki.getdoc(add) directly without registration to obtain enriched YAML. Documentation generators can also use the static enrichment API.

docs.title: Synchronize, format and validate source
docs.text:
pip install douki

douki sync src/            # Add missing descriptions
douki format src/          # Normalize YAML formatting
douki format --check src/  # Preview formatting differences
douki check src/           # Validate documentation

check and sync require annotations for parameters, return values and documented attributes. Use -> None for functions without a result; implicit method receivers are exempt. Authored type fields are rejected by the schema. Remove only those fields from existing docstrings and put types in annotations instead. Keep parameters, returns and attributes with their descriptions: annotations supply types, not explanations.

sync adds missing parameter, attribute and return entries with ... placeholders, without storing types. It preserves existing descriptions and reports stale parameter names. format only changes presentation; check reports missing or incomplete descriptions. Dynamic inspection raises DocumentationError for missing annotations.

The CLI can remain a development dependency. Install Douki in the running interpreter when using getdoc, help or library registration.

Documentation generators can use the public enrich, Signature and Parameter API with statically collected types, without importing the project being documented. See the usage guide.

Douki respects .gitignore by default. Override it with --no-respect-gitignore or [tool.douki] respect-gitignore = false.

  • fix(benchmarks): keep ASV comparisons compatible with upstream

Add regressions for the missing API and current enrichment path, remove duplicate fixture keys, and document benchmark compatibility rules.

Keep documented instance annotations visible to runtime inspection. Extend regressions to verify descriptions survive source formatting, static metadata enrichment, getdoc, and help.

Validation: makim tests.ci (233 tests, smoke checks, pre-commit) and makim docs.build.

  • refactor: rename help activation to enable and disable

Use douki.enable() and douki.disable() consistently in public exports, lazy loading, documentation, and tests. Preserve idempotent activation and restoration of the previous help function.

Validation: makim tests.ci (233 passed, smoke and pre-commit checks) and makim docs.build.

  • refactor(docs): simplify authored return descriptions

Use return description strings throughout source docstrings, examples, and benchmarks. Keep nested descriptions accepted and generated output expanded with annotation-derived types.

Emit string returns during NumPy migration. Preserve indentation relative to section headings so standalone return prose is not mistaken for a type entry and discarded. Cover multiline prose, quoting, and type-only entries.

Importing the library installs help routing once; only declarations owned by registered packages and their dotted descendants receive enrichment. Unregistered objects go directly to the original helper before Douki YAML or signature inspection, including dependency re-exports and inherited foreign methods. Mixed dispatch variants and class attribute owners obey the same boundary. Preserve later help wrappers on repeated registration.

Keep getdoc and static enrichment independent of registration and leave stored docstrings unchanged. Update public exports, examples, and usage.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
In order to be able to contribute, it is important that you understand the project layout.

This project uses the src layout, which means that the package code is located at ./src/douki.

For my information, check the official documentation: https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/

In addition, you should know that to build our package we use Poetry, it's a Python package management tool that simplifies the process of building and publishing Python packages. It allows us to easily manage dependencies, virtual environments and package versions. Poetry also includes features such as dependency resolution, lock files and publishing to PyPI. Overall, Poetry streamlines the process of managing Python packages, making it easier for us to create and share our code with others.

Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little bit helps, and credit will always be given.

You can contribute in many ways:

• douki uses a set of pre-commit hooks to improve code quality. The hooks can be installed locally using:

docs.title: Release
docs.text: This project uses semantic-release in order to cut a new release based on the commit-message.

docs.title: Commit message format
docs.text:
semantic-release uses the commit messages to determine the consumer impact of changes in the codebase. Following formalized conventions for commit messages, semantic-release automatically determines the next semantic version number, generates a changelog and publishes the release.

By default, semantic-release uses Angular Commit Message Conventions. The commit message format can be changed with the preset or config options_ of the @semantic-release/commit-analyzer and @semantic-release/release-notes-generator plugins.

Tools such as commitizen or commitlint can be used to help contributors and enforce valid commit messages.

The table below shows which commit message gets you which release type when semantic-release runs (using the default configuration):

Commit message Release type fix(pencil): stop graphite breaking when pressure is applied Fix Release feat(pencil): add 'graphiteWidth' option Feature Release perf(pencil): remove graphiteWidth option Chore feat(pencil)!: The graphiteWidth option has been removed Breaking Release

Note: For a breaking change release, uses ! at the end of the message prefix.

source: https://github.com/semantic-release/semantic-release/blob/master/README.md#commit-message-format

As this project uses the squash and merge strategy, ensure to apply the commit message format to the PR's title.

docs.title: Performance benchmarks
docs.text: Douki tracks synchronization and file-discovery performance with Airspeed Velocity (ASV). The first benchmarks cover validation of a single YAML docstring, syncing one docstring, syncing Python modules with 25 and 250 functions, and discovering Python files across a large ignored directory.

docs.title: Local use
docs.text:
Install Douki and ASV in a Python 3.11 environment:

python -m pip install -e .
python -m pip install "asv==0.6.5" "virtualenv>=20"
asv check -E existing
asv machine --yes

Quick feedback when developing a new benchmark (not a timing baseline):

asv run -E existing --quick --show-stderr

Compare the current branch against the current upstream main in isolated environments, using the same machine for both revisions:

git fetch upstream main
asv continuous --interleave-rounds --show-stderr upstream/main HEAD

Run and record a proper historical benchmark:

asv run HEAD^!
asv publish
asv preview

ASV stores results under .asv/results. See the ASV documentation for detailed usage.

docs.title: GitHub Actions: PR comparison and comment
docs.text:
Every PR targeting main gets a performance comparison. The compare-pr-performance CI job checks out the exact PR head, benchmarks it against the exact upstream base commit with asv continuous, and creates a Markdown report with one row per benchmark:

Benchmark main PR Time change Speedup Assessment Example sync 10 ms 5 ms -50.0% 2.00× Faster

The values above are illustrative, not measured Douki results. The actual comment uses the recorded ASV measurements. It also includes the compared commit hashes, a summary of regressions/improvements, and a link to the run logs and full artifact. Each new PR push updates the existing comment instead of generating a new one.

Pull requests from forks do not receive a write-capable GitHub token. Therefore the benchmarking job uses read-only credentials, uploads the report, and a small trusted workflow_run workflow posts the comment on the same PR with issues: write. It never checks out or runs PR code. This is a security boundary, not a post-merge-only performance check. The reporter must exist on upstream main to be enabled; when first introducing these workflows, the initial PR can generate an artifact but its comment reporter will become active after the workflow is merged. Subsequent PRs get the automatic comments.

Performance regressions are advisory and do not block PRs; benchmark execution failures are reported as failures rather than silently passing. Both commits run on one runner to limit hardware differences.

docs.title: Historical benchmarks
docs.text:
• Pushes to upstream main: ASV records the current commit, restores previous records, and stores the updated JSON result history on the benchmark-results branch, separate from documentation publishing.
  • Weekly: the same historical benchmark is rerun on Monday.
  • Pull-request performance is advisory: shared GitHub-hosted runners vary in CPU characteristics and load. A large change deserves a second run and/or controlled dedicated-machine verification before it becomes a release-blocking regression.

The dedicated benchmark-results branch holds committed ASV JSON history. It can be fetched and copied into .asv/results to generate a local ASV dashboard using asv publish. The branch is created by the first successful upstream history run. The repository's CI benchmark uses Python 3.11 to keep cost manageable; functionality continues to be tested across Python 3.10 through 3.14 by the existing test matrix.

docs.title: Benchmark maintenance
docs.text:
Benchmarks should use deterministic, offline fixtures and exclude fixture construction from timed functions. Include representative large-repository cases as well as single-docstring cases. If the benchmark suite evolves, ASV can compare only the cases that exist in both revisions; changes to benchmark definitions should be clearly identified in the PR discussion.

ASV loads the current benchmark definitions against both installed revisions. Keep module-level imports compatible with the baseline. Benchmarks for new APIs belong in a separate class whose setup() checks for the API and raises NotImplementedError when it is unavailable. This skips only that benchmark on older revisions; shared benchmarks must still run and produce comparable measurements. The report shows new-API rows as n/a on the baseline instead of treating them as speed improvements.

Do not update poetry.lock solely for ASV: it is installed by the dedicated performance workflow and is not a runtime dependency.

docs.title: Authoring
docs.text:
Put types in annotations and descriptions in Douki YAML:

def greet(name: str, times: int = 1) -> str:
    """
    title: Greet someone.
    parameters:
      name: Person to greet.
      times: Number of greetings.
    returns: The greeting text.
    """
    return "\n".join([f"Hello, {name}!"] * times)

A title is required. Parameter entries can be description strings or mappings with description, default, optional and variadic. Write parameter and return descriptions in the docstring, as above. Annotations supply the types; Douki does not infer these descriptions. Use a string for returns, or a YAML block scalar for longer text:

returns: >-
  The greeting text, with one greeting per line.
  Each greeting includes the supplied name.

Generated help and API documentation expand this to a mapping with description and the annotation-derived type. Existing nested returns: {description: ...} entries remain supported.

Authored type fields are forbidden. The shipped douki/schema.json defines all supported fields, including attributes, raises, yields, examples and notes. Use plain parameter names for variadics (args, not *args).

docs.title: Formatting and validation
docs.text:
douki sync src/            # Scaffold missing descriptions
douki format src/          # Format YAML presentation
douki format --check src/  # Preview formatting changes
douki check src/           # Validate documentation
douki check                # Validate files in the current directory

sync adds missing parameter, attribute and result descriptions as ... placeholders without writing type fields. It preserves authored entries and reports stale parameters instead of removing them. format normalizes YAML formatting, shortening description-only parameter and attribute mappings to strings while retaining entries with extra fields; format --check checks presentation without writing. check validates schemas, annotations, stale names and missing or placeholder descriptions. Both sync and check require annotated parameters and return values; use -> None when a function returns nothing. Only the actual method receiver is exempt; a static method's first argument still requires an annotation, even when named self or cls.

Documented attributes require annotation metadata too. Class and module annotations and property getter return annotations supply these types. Source checks also validate instance fields collected from __init__. Declare instance attributes at class scope when runtime help must find them:

class Counter:
    """
    title: A counter.
    attributes:
      count: Current value.
    """
    count: int

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """title: Initialize the counter."""
        self.count = 0

An annotation only inside a method is not retained in the class's runtime metadata. Douki does not guess types from attribute values or instantiate classes to discover fields. Static adapters must supply inherited attribute annotations; the Python CLI resolves inheritance from earlier same-file classes, not imported bases. An explicit local annotation avoids ambiguity. Validation requires annotation presence, not proof of type correctness; use a type checker such as mypy for that.

Exit code Meaning 0 No changes needed 1 Formatting differs (check) or was updated (sync) 2 Invalid docstrings or another processing error

Migrating from earlier Douki releases: remove type fields from parameters, attributes, returns, yields and receives, and add any missing annotations. Keep the sections and their descriptions. If an entry previously contained only a type, replace that field with a description of the value's purpose. Expanded docstrings from older releases are no longer valid source input. Neither sync nor check silently discards those fields. Replace typed lists in raises and warnings with mappings, for example raises: {ValueError: Invalid value.}. Exception and warning names remain authored because Python has no corresponding declaration annotations.

The explicit douki.sync.sync_docstring API still generates expanded output from annotation metadata for legacy consumers. Its input must follow the source schema, and supplied parameters and attributes must be annotated. An empty parameter list and empty return annotation represent a non-callable declaration in that legacy API; use Signature for an unambiguous contract. Expanded output is a rendered view, not valid source input for a second pass.

docs.title: Dynamic help
docs.text:
Register each participating library once from its __init__.py:

# mylib/__init__.py
import douki

douki.register(__name__)

Consumers only need to import the library:

import json
import mylib

help(mylib.greet)  # Descriptions and types from mylib's annotations
help(json.dumps)  # Regular Python help

register accepts a full module or package name. Registration is idempotent and covers that exact name and its dotted descendants, including submodules imported later. Registering mylib does not include mylib_extra or unrelated packages sharing a namespace. Each library can register independently. Names are validated before registration; no modules are imported by this call.

The first registration installs a shared builtins.help wrapper. It checks the object's defining module before inspecting Douki documentation. Functions re-exported from unregistered dependencies, inherited foreign methods, and foreign dispatch implementations retain standard Python documentation. Class attribute enrichment also respects declaring owners. Objects without Douki docstrings use the original helper, even inside a registered package.

Importing Douki alone does not install the wrapper. There are no enable or disable calls for consumers. Subsequent registrations preserve any help wrapper installed by another tool after Douki. help() with no argument and string requests such as help("keywords") use the original helper; that interactive topic session does not automatically enrich its requests. Call help(object) for package-scoped object documentation. douki.help uses the same routing rules.

Explicit inspection does not require registration:

text = douki.getdoc(greet)

getdoc returns enriched YAML for Douki docstrings, ordinary cleaned text for other docstrings, and None when documentation is absent. It never changes __doc__, annotations or function identity. Repeated calls derive the result from current metadata, so no cached types become stale. This explicit API works on objects from any package and does not install or consult the help registry.

Class and module help includes members; property getters are never called. Module __all__ exports are respected. Plum dispatch implementations retain separate types. On Python 3.11+, registered typing.overload declarations also retain separate types, inheriting implementation prose when needed. On Python 3.10 only the runtime implementation signature is available for typing.overload. getdoc separates multiple variants with YAML --- document separators.

Python 3.10–3.13 use unevaluated string annotations when present; Python 3.14 uses annotationlib's string format. Douki does not call typing.get_type_hints to resolve missing type-only imports. Runtime inspection is for code already imported in the current interpreter. Generator return annotations describe the returned iterator, including its yield/send types when supplied through Generator or AsyncGenerator. The yields and receives sections contain descriptions only; Douki does not decompose the generator annotation into separate fields.

docs.title: Static documentation generators
docs.text:
The shared API accepts strings and typed metadata. An adapter such as DoukiMD's Griffe collector can supply this without importing project code, registering a package, or changing Python help:

from douki import Parameter, Signature, enrich, format_documentation

signature = Signature(
    parameters=(Parameter("name", "str"), Parameter("times", "int")),
    returns="str",
)
data = enrich(
    "title: Greet someone\n"
    "parameters:\n"
    "  name: Person to greet.\n"
    "  times: Number of greetings.\n"
    "returns: The greeting text.\n",
    signature,
)
text = format_documentation(data, enriched=True)

data is a validated documentation mapping that renderers can consume directly. Types come exclusively from annotations. Descriptions and other metadata survive enrichment. Missing annotations raise DocumentationError with phase annotations, listing all missing fields for that declaration. Unknown documented parameters and duplicate signature names raise DocumentationError with a processing phase. Invalid metadata types raise Typeguard errors, including invalid items later in a collection. format_documentation validates source YAML by default; enriched=True explicitly permits generated type fields. The generated view must not be written back into source or passed back into enrich as authored input. validate_annotations(signature, documentation) exposes the same presence checks for adapters that already hold schema-validated documentation.

Use parameters=None for non-callable declarations, parameters=() for a function with no arguments, and attributes=(Parameter(...), ...) for class/module attributes. Adapters supply each overload separately and omit implicit receivers. kind accepts regular, positional_only, keyword_only, var_positional and var_keyword.

This API enables a DoukiMD integration; installing this Douki version does not by itself change DoukiMD's collector.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
douki migrate --from numpydoc src/

Migration converts NumPy-style descriptions into type-free YAML. Add Python annotations first: migration never invents them from prose and fails without writing the affected file when annotations are missing. It preserves exception/warning names as mapping keys. Follow with douki check src/.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
You can configure Douki using a pyproject.toml file in your project root. Douki supports excluding files or directories using glob patterns, and it respects .gitignore during file discovery by default.

[tool.douki]
# Respect `.gitignore` by default. Set to false to opt out globally.
respect-gitignore = true

# Exclude specific files or entire directories
exclude = [
  "tests/smoke/*",
  "legacy_module.py"
]

When running douki sync, douki check, or douki migrate, any file matching these patterns will be ignored. You can override the .gitignore setting for a single run with --respect-gitignore or --no-respect-gitignore.

docs.title: Pre-commit integration
docs.text:
With Douki installed in your development environment:

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: douki
        name: Format Douki docstrings
        entry: douki sync
        language: system
        types: [python]

Use douki check instead when the hook should report differences without writing files.

@public
@typechecked
def enrich(raw_docstring: str, signature: Signature) -> dict[str, object]:
    """
    title: Return structured documentation enriched with
      annotation types.
    summary: Types come exclusively from annotations. No
      objects or source files are modified. Missing annotations
      raise DocumentationError.
    parameters:
      raw_docstring: >-
        Authored Douki YAML containing descriptions and no
        type fields.
      signature: Annotation metadata supplied by the language
        adapter.
    returns: >-
      New documentation mapping with authored descriptions
      and annotation-derived types.
    """
    try:
        try:
            # Already-cleaned YAML must retain its significant indentation.
            parsed = _parse_validated_docstring(raw_docstring)
        except ValueError:
            # Raw Python docstrings may still need indentation cleanup.
            parsed = _parse_validated_docstring(
                inspect.cleandoc(raw_docstring)
            )
        data = normalize_documentation(cast(dict[str, object], parsed))
    except ValueError as error:
        raise DocumentationError('schema', str(error)) from error
    validate_annotations(signature, data)
    if signature.parameters is not None:
        parameters = merge_fields(
            cast(dict[str, object], data.get('parameters', {})),
            signature.parameters,
            strict=True,
        )
        if parameters or 'parameters' in data:
            data['parameters'] = parameters
    if signature.attributes:
        data['attributes'] = merge_fields(
            cast(dict[str, object], data.get('attributes', {})),
            signature.attributes,
            strict=False,
        )
    if signature.returns:
        returns = entry(data.get('returns'))
        returns['type'] = signature.returns
        data['returns'] = returns
    return data

def format_documentation(
    data: dict[str, object],
    *,
    width: int = 79,
    enriched: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Serialize validated source or explicitly enriched documentation.
    summary: Only generated output may contain annotation-derived type fields.
    parameters:
      data: Documentation mapping to validate and serialize.
      width: Target line width for the serialized YAML.
      enriched: >-
        Whether to allow annotation-derived type fields in generated output.
    returns: Serialized YAML with canonical field order and preserved values.
    """
    try:
        validate_schema(data, enriched=enriched)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise DocumentationError('schema', str(error)) from error
    ordered = {key: data[key] for key in _KEY_ORDER if key in data}
    target = max(20, width)
    wrap_width = target
    for _ in range(4):
        text = yaml.dump(
            ordered,
            Dumper=DocumentationDumper,
            sort_keys=False,
            allow_unicode=True,
            width=wrap_width,
        )
        # PyYAML treats width as a hint and can overshoot by one word.
        excess = max(
            (len(line) - target for line in text.splitlines()), default=0
        )
        if excess <= 0 or wrap_width == 20:
            break
        wrap_width = max(20, wrap_width - max(excess, 8))
    return text

@typechecked
def getdoc(obj: object, *, skip_receiver: bool = False) -> str | None:
    """
    title: Return enriched Douki YAML or an ordinary cleaned docstring.
    summary: The object's original __doc__ is never changed.
    parameters:
      obj: Declaration whose documentation or annotation metadata is needed.
      skip_receiver: Whether to omit the first parameter of an unbound method.
    returns: >-
      Enriched Douki YAML, cleaned ordinary prose, or None when no docstring
      exists.
    """
    alternatives = variants(obj)
    if len(alternatives) > 1 or alternatives[0] is not obj:
        documents = [
            variant_doc(variant, obj, skip_receiver)
            for variant in alternatives
        ]
        return '\n---\n'.join(doc for doc in documents if doc) or None
    raw = inspect.getdoc(obj)
    if raw is None:
        return None
    # Ordinary prose remains ordinary prose. A title key opts into Douki.
    if not is_douki(raw):
        return raw
    return format_documentation(
        enrich(raw, metadata(obj, skip_receiver)), enriched=True
    )

def register(package: str) -> None:
    """
    title: Register a library for annotation-enriched help.
    summary: Call once from the library's __init__.py using __name__.
      Registration includes future submodules without importing them.
      Other packages continue to use the previously installed help
      helper.
    parameters:
      package: Full module or package import name to register.
    raises:
      DocumentationError: The name is empty or is not a dotted identifier.
    """
    global fallback_help
    if not all(part.isidentifier() for part in package.split('.')):
        raise DocumentationError('registration', 'Expected a dotted name')
    # Install once. A later helper may delegate back to ours, so capturing
    # it again would create a recursion cycle or overwrite another hook.
    if not registered_packages and builtins.help is not help:
        fallback_help = builtins.help
        setattr(builtins, 'help', help)
    registered_packages.add(package)

@public
@typechecked
def validate_annotations(
    signature: Signature,
    documentation: dict[str, object] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    title: Require explicit annotations at the shared documentation boundary.
    summary: Adapters omit implicit method receivers from parameter metadata.
      Documented attributes must have declarations; values are never used
      to guess their types.
    parameters:
      signature: Annotation metadata supplied by the language adapter.
      documentation: >-
        Authored mapping used to check that documented attributes are declared.
    """
    missing: list[str] = []
    if signature.parameters is not None:
        missing.extend(
            f"parameter '{parameter.name}'"
            for parameter in signature.parameters
            if not parameter.annotation.strip().strip('\'"').strip()
        )
        if not signature.returns.strip().strip('\'"').strip():
            missing.append('return value (use -> None for no result)')
    attributes = {item.name: item.annotation for item in signature.attributes}
    documented = (documentation or {}).get('attributes', {})
    if isinstance(documented, dict):
        for name in documented:
            attributes.setdefault(name, '')
    missing.extend(
        f"attribute '{name}'"
        for name, annotation in attributes.items()
        if not annotation.strip().strip('\'"').strip()
    )
    if missing:
        raise DocumentationError(
            'annotations',
            'Missing type annotations: ' + ', '.join(missing),
        )

def format_documentation(
    data: dict[str, object],
    *,
    width: int = 79,
    enriched: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Serialize validated source or explicitly enriched documentation.
    summary: Only generated output may contain annotation-derived type fields.
    parameters:
      data: Documentation mapping to validate and serialize.
      width: Target line width for the serialized YAML.
      enriched: >-
        Whether to allow annotation-derived type fields in generated output.
    returns: Serialized YAML with canonical field order and preserved values.
    """
    try:
        validate_schema(data, enriched=enriched)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise DocumentationError('schema', str(error)) from error
    ordered = {key: data[key] for key in _KEY_ORDER if key in data}
    target = max(20, width)
    wrap_width = target
    for _ in range(4):
        text = yaml.dump(
            ordered,
            Dumper=DocumentationDumper,
            sort_keys=False,
            allow_unicode=True,
            width=wrap_width,
        )
        # PyYAML treats width as a hint and can overshoot by one word.
        excess = max(
            (len(line) - target for line in text.splitlines()), default=0
        )
        if excess <= 0 or wrap_width == 20:
            break
        wrap_width = max(20, wrap_width - max(excess, 8))
    return text

def merge_fields(
    existing: dict[str, object],
    parameters: tuple[Parameter, ...],
    *,
    strict: bool,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """
    title: Merge annotation types without deleting descriptions.
    parameters:
      existing: Authored entries keyed by parameter or attribute name.
      parameters: Annotated fields to merge with their authored descriptions.
      strict: Whether to reject authored names absent from the signature.
    returns: >-
      New field mapping combining descriptions with annotation-derived types.
    """
    names = {parameter.name for parameter in parameters}
    if strict and (unknown := set(existing) - names):
        raise DocumentationError(
            'signature',
            'Unknown documented parameters: ' + ', '.join(sorted(unknown)),
        )
    result = dict(existing)
    for parameter in parameters:
        field = entry(existing.get(parameter.name))
        if parameter.annotation:
            field['type'] = parameter.annotation
        if parameter.kind == 'var_positional':
            field['variadic'] = 'positional'
        elif parameter.kind == 'var_keyword':
            field['variadic'] = 'keyword'
        if field or parameter.name in existing:
            result[parameter.name] = field
    return result

                    value,

                    prefix_length=4 + len(name),

            elif isinstance(value, dict):

                if isinstance(description, str):
                    field['description'] = description_style(
                        description,
                        width=width,
                        prefix_length=17,
                    )
                styled[name] = field
            else:
                styled[name] = value
        result[section] = styled

    for section in ('returns', 'yields', 'receives'):
        value = data.get(section)
        if isinstance(value, str):
            result[section] = description_style(
                value,
                width=width,
                prefix_length=len(section) + 2,
            )
        elif isinstance(value, dict):

            description = field.get('description')
            if isinstance(description, str):
                field['description'] = description_style(
                    description,

                    prefix_length=15,
                )

@public
@typechecked
def validate_annotations(
    signature: Signature,
    documentation: dict[str, object] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    title: Require explicit annotations at the shared documentation boundary.
    summary: Adapters omit implicit method receivers from parameter metadata.
      Documented attributes must have declarations; values are never used
      to guess their types.
    parameters:
      signature: Annotation metadata supplied by the language adapter.
      documentation: >-
        Authored mapping used to check that documented attributes are declared.
    """
    missing: list[str] = []
    if signature.parameters is not None:
        missing.extend(
            f"parameter '{parameter.name}'"
            for parameter in signature.parameters
            if not parameter.annotation.strip().strip('\'"').strip()
        )
        if not signature.returns.strip().strip('\'"').strip():
            missing.append('return value (use -> None for no result)')
    attributes = {item.name: item.annotation for item in signature.attributes}
    documented = (documentation or {}).get('attributes', {})
    if isinstance(documented, dict):
        for name in documented:
            attributes.setdefault(name, '')
    missing.extend(
        f"attribute '{name}'"
        for name, annotation in attributes.items()
        if not annotation.strip().strip('\'"').strip()
    )
    if missing:
        raise DocumentationError(
            'annotations',
            'Missing type annotations: ' + ', '.join(missing),
        )

@dispatch
@typechecked
def visit(
    self,
    obj: type | ModuleType,
    name: str,
    skip_receiver: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Include documented members and guard against recursive aliases.
    parameters:
      obj: Object whose documentation or members are being inspected.
      name: Display name for the object in the rendered help.
      skip_receiver: >-
        Whether to omit the first parameter of an unbound method.
    returns: Help text for the object and any supported documented members.
    """
    if id(obj) in self.seen:
        return f'{name} (already documented)'
    self.seen.add(id(obj))
    raw = own_doc(obj)
    documentation = (
        render_doc(obj, raw)
        if raw is not None and is_douki(raw)
        else inspect.getdoc(obj) or ''
    )
    sections = [name, documentation]
    for member_name, member, skip in members(obj):
        if contains_douki(member, set()):
            sections.append(self.visit(member, member_name, skip))
        else:
            sections.append(
                str(
                    pydoc.plaintext.document(
                        member,
                        member_name,
                    )
                )
            )
    return '\n\n'.join(section for section in sections if section)

@private
@typechecked
def contains_douki(obj: object, seen: set[int]) -> bool:
    """
    title: Leave ordinary Python help unchanged outside documented objects.
    parameters:
      obj: Object whose documentation or members are being inspected.
      seen: Visited object identities, updated to prevent recursive traversal.
    returns: >-
      Whether the object or any inspected member contains Douki documentation.
    """
    if not is_registered(obj) or id(obj) in seen:
        return False
    seen.add(id(obj))
    alternatives = variants(obj)
    if len(alternatives) > 1 or alternatives[0] is not obj:
        return any(
            is_registered(item) and is_douki(variant_text(item, obj))
            for item in alternatives
        )
    if is_douki(own_doc(obj)):
        return True
    if isinstance(obj, (type, ModuleType)):
        return any(contains_douki(item, seen) for _, item, _ in members(obj))
    return False

@private

def members(obj: type | ModuleType) -> list[tuple[str, object, bool]]:
    """
    title: Read container members without evaluating property descriptors.
    parameters:
      obj: Object whose documentation or members are being inspected.
    returns: >-
      Member names, objects, and flags indicating implicit method receivers.
    """
    values: dict[str, object] = {}
    if isinstance(obj, type):
        for owner in reversed(obj.__mro__[:-1]):
            values.update(vars(owner))
    else:
        values.update(vars(obj))
    exports = values.get('__all__') if isinstance(obj, ModuleType) else None
    result: list[tuple[str, object, bool]] = []
    for name, value in values.items():
        if isinstance(obj, ModuleType):
            if isinstance(exports, (list, tuple)):
                if name not in exports:
                    continue
            elif getattr(value, '__module__', None) != obj.__name__:
                continue
        skip = isinstance(obj, type) and isinstance(
            value,
            (FunctionType, Function),
        )
        if isinstance(value, (staticmethod, classmethod)):
            skip = isinstance(value, classmethod)
            value = value.__func__
        if (
            isinstance(value, (Function, type, property))
            or inspect.isroutine(value)
            or isinstance(exports, (list, tuple))
        ):
            result.append((name, value, skip))
    return result

def register(package: str) -> None:
    """
    title: Register a library for annotation-enriched help.
    summary: Call once from the library's __init__.py using __name__.
      Registration includes future submodules without importing them.
      Other packages continue to use the previously installed help
      helper.
    parameters:
      package: Full module or package import name to register.
    raises:
      DocumentationError: The name is empty or is not a dotted identifier.
    """
    global fallback_help
    if not all(part.isidentifier() for part in package.split('.')):
        raise DocumentationError('registration', 'Expected a dotted name')
    # Install once. A later helper may delegate back to ours, so capturing
    # it again would create a recursion cycle or overwrite another hook.
    if not registered_packages and builtins.help is not help:
        fallback_help = builtins.help
        setattr(builtins, 'help', help)
    registered_packages.add(package)

@private
@typechecked
def attributes(
    obj: type | ModuleType,
    *,
    include: Callable[[object], bool] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Parameter, ...]:
    """
    title: Read declared attributes without evaluating forward references.
    parameters:
      obj: Declaration whose documentation or annotation metadata
        is needed.
      include: >-
        Optional filter for declaring classes, modules, and property
        getters; None includes every owner.
    returns: >-
      Declared attribute annotations, including inherited fields
      and properties.
    """
    owners = reversed(obj.__mro__) if isinstance(obj, type) else [obj]
    result: dict[str, Parameter] = {}
    for owner in owners:
        if sys.version_info >= (3, 14):
            import annotationlib

            annotations = annotationlib.get_annotations(
                owner,
                format=annotationlib.Format.STRING,
            )
        else:
            annotations = inspect.get_annotations(owner, eval_str=False)
        if include is not None and not include(owner):
            # Foreign overrides hide included declarations without
            # validating their annotations or inspecting property getters.
            for name in set(vars(owner)) | set(annotations):
                result.pop(name, None)
            continue
        for name, value in annotations.items():
            result[name] = Parameter(name, display_annotation(value))
        for name, value in vars(owner).items():
            if isinstance(value, property):
                if include is not None and not include(value):
                    result.pop(name, None)
                    continue
                annotation = (
                    display_annotation(
                        callable_signature(value.fget).return_annotation
                    )
                    if value.fget is not None
                    else ''
                )
                result[name] = Parameter(name, annotation)
    return tuple(result.values())

    parameters:

                parameter.name,
                display_annotation(parameter.annotation),
                kinds[parameter.kind],
            )
            for parameter in values
        ),
        returns=display_annotation(signature.return_annotation),

@private
@typechecked
def variants(obj: object) -> tuple[object, ...]:
    """
    title: Retain distinct typing overloads and Plum implementations.
    parameters:
      obj: Declaration whose documentation or annotation metadata is needed.
    returns: >-
      Distinct overload implementations, or the original object as a single
      item.
    """
    target = obj.__func__ if isinstance(obj, MethodType) else obj
    if isinstance(obj, Function) or (
        isinstance(obj, MethodType) and hasattr(target, 'methods')
    ):
        methods = getattr(target, 'methods')
        if not isinstance(methods, Sequence) or not all(
            isinstance(method, Method) for method in methods
        ):
            raise DocumentationError('signature', 'Invalid dispatch methods')
        implementations = tuple(
            dict.fromkeys(method.implementation for method in methods)
        )
        if not implementations:
            raise DocumentationError('signature', 'No dispatch methods')
        if isinstance(obj, MethodType):
            return tuple(MethodType(f, obj.__self__) for f in implementations)
        return implementations
    if isinstance(target, FunctionType) and hasattr(typing, 'get_overloads'):
        overloads = typing.get_overloads(target)
        if overloads:
            if isinstance(obj, MethodType):
                return tuple(MethodType(f, obj.__self__) for f in overloads)
            return tuple(overloads)
    return (obj,)

def sync_docstring(
    raw_docstring: str,
    params: Sequence[ParamInfo],
    return_annotation: str,
    *,
    attrs: Sequence[ParamInfo] = (),
    func_name: str = '<unknown>',
    content_indent: int = 4,
    language_defaults: Optional[LanguageDefaults] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Merge signature info into a Douki YAML docstring.
    summary: Returns the updated YAML (without surrounding triple-quotes).
      If not valid Douki YAML, raises ValueError.
    parameters:
      raw_docstring: Authored Douki YAML without surrounding string
        delimiters.
      params: Parameter metadata extracted from the declaration signature.
      return_annotation: Return annotation supplied by the language
        adapter.
      attrs: >-
        Class-level annotated variables used to sync the attributes:
        section. Only meaningful for ClassDef docstrings.
      func_name: >-
        Declaration name retained for compatibility with existing
        callers.
      content_indent: Source indentation width to allow for when
        wrapping YAML.
      language_defaults: Language-specific values to omit from generated
        YAML.
    returns: >-
      Annotation-enriched YAML for display, without surrounding string
      delimiters.
    """
    # Keep func_name in the public API for compatibility.
    _ = func_name
    if not raw_docstring or not raw_docstring.strip():
        return raw_docstring

    data = _parse_validated_docstring(raw_docstring)
    from douki.documentation import Parameter, Signature, validate_annotations

    validate_annotations(
        Signature(
            parameters=(
                tuple(Parameter(p.name, p.annotation) for p in params)
                if params or return_annotation
                else None
            ),
            returns=return_annotation,
            attributes=tuple(Parameter(p.name, p.annotation) for p in attrs),
        ),
        data,
    )
    return _sync_docstring_data(
        data,
        params,
        return_annotation,
        attrs=attrs,
        content_indent=content_indent,
        language_defaults=language_defaults,
    )

def collect_source_files(
    paths: list[Path],
    *,
    file_extensions: tuple[str, ...],
    discovery: DiscoveryConfig,
) -> list[Path]:
    """
    title: Expand paths into source files using shared discovery rules.
    parameters:
      paths: Files or directories to expand into source files.
      file_extensions: Filename suffixes accepted by the language backend.
      discovery: >-
        Project root and exclusion settings used during file discovery.
    returns: Sorted, unique source paths after applying exclusion rules.
    """
    matcher = _GitIgnoreMatcher(discovery.root)
    result: list[Path] = []

    for path in paths:
        if path.is_dir():
            # Top-down traversal lets us skip excluded subtrees entirely.
            for root, directories, filenames in os.walk(path):
                parent = Path(root)
                directories[:] = [
                    name
                    for name in directories
                    if not _can_prune_directory(
                        parent / name,
                        discovery=discovery,
                        matcher=matcher,
                    )
                ]
                for name in filenames:
                    child = parent / name
                    if (
                        child.is_file()
                        and _matches_extension(child, file_extensions)
                        and not _is_excluded(
                            child, discovery=discovery, matcher=matcher
                        )
                    ):
                        result.append(child)
            continue

        if _matches_extension(path, file_extensions) and not _is_excluded(
            path,
            discovery=discovery,
            matcher=matcher,
        ):
            result.append(path)

    return sorted(set(result))

def load_douki_discovery_config(cwd: Path) -> DiscoveryConfig:
    """
    title: Load shared discovery settings from `pyproject.toml`.
    parameters:
      cwd: Starting directory for the upward project configuration search.
    returns: Nearest project discovery settings, or defaults rooted at cwd.
    """
    curr = cwd.resolve()
    while True:
        pyproject = curr / 'pyproject.toml'
        if pyproject.is_file():
            return _load_pyproject_discovery_config(pyproject)
        parent = curr.parent
        if parent == curr:
            break
        curr = parent
    return DiscoveryConfig(root=cwd.resolve())

def compact_documentation(
    documentation: dict[str, object],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """
    title: Shorten description-only parameter and attribute entries.
    summary: Format output without changing the original input mapping.
    parameters:
      documentation: Validated authored documentation to format.
    returns: A copy with description-only mappings replaced by strings.

        fields = result.get(section)

            continue

            name: value['description']

def normalize_documentation(
    documentation: dict[str, object],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """
    title: Normalize parameter and attribute shorthand in memory.
    summary: The authored mapping and its nested entries remain unchanged.
    parameters:
      documentation: Parsed, schema-validated source documentation.
    returns: A copy with string entries represented by description mappings.
    """
    result = dict(documentation)
    for section in ('parameters', 'attributes'):
        entries = result.get(section)
        if entries is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(entries, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"schema: '{section}' must be a mapping")
        normalized: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
        for name, value in entries.items():
            if not isinstance(name, str):
                raise ValueError(f"schema: invalid '{section}' name")
            if isinstance(value, str):
                normalized[name] = {'description': value}
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                if not all(isinstance(key, str) for key in value):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"schema: invalid '{section}' entry '{name}'"
                    )
                normalized[name] = dict(value)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"schema: invalid '{section}' entry '{name}'")
        result[section] = normalized
    return result

def sync_docstring(
    raw_docstring: str,
    params: Sequence[ParamInfo],
    return_annotation: str,
    *,
    attrs: Sequence[ParamInfo] = (),
    func_name: str = '<unknown>',
    content_indent: int = 4,
    language_defaults: Optional[LanguageDefaults] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Merge signature info into a Douki YAML docstring.
    summary: Returns the updated YAML (without surrounding triple-quotes).
      If not valid Douki YAML, raises ValueError.
    parameters:
      raw_docstring: Authored Douki YAML without surrounding string
        delimiters.
      params: Parameter metadata extracted from the declaration signature.
      return_annotation: Return annotation supplied by the language
        adapter.
      attrs: >-
        Class-level annotated variables used to sync the attributes:
        section. Only meaningful for ClassDef docstrings.
      func_name: >-
        Declaration name retained for compatibility with existing
        callers.
      content_indent: Source indentation width to allow for when
        wrapping YAML.
      language_defaults: Language-specific values to omit from generated
        YAML.
    returns: >-
      Annotation-enriched YAML for display, without surrounding string
      delimiters.
    """
    # Keep func_name in the public API for compatibility.
    _ = func_name
    if not raw_docstring or not raw_docstring.strip():
        return raw_docstring

    data = _parse_validated_docstring(raw_docstring)
    from douki.documentation import Parameter, Signature, validate_annotations

    validate_annotations(
        Signature(
            parameters=(
                tuple(Parameter(p.name, p.annotation) for p in params)
                if params or return_annotation
                else None
            ),
            returns=return_annotation,
            attributes=tuple(Parameter(p.name, p.annotation) for p in attrs),
        ),
        data,
    )
    return _sync_docstring_data(
        data,
        params,
        return_annotation,
        attrs=attrs,
        content_indent=content_indent,
        language_defaults=language_defaults,
    )

def body_nodes(statements: list[ast.stmt]) -> Iterator[ast.AST]:
    """
    title: Walk a declaration's body without entering nested scopes.
    parameters:
      statements: Statements in the declaration body to traverse.
    returns: >-
      Iterator over body nodes, leaving nested declaration bodies unvisited.
    """
    pending: list[ast.AST] = list(reversed(statements))
    while pending:
        node = pending.pop()
        yield node
        if not isinstance(
            node,
            (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef, ast.Lambda),
        ):
            pending.extend(reversed(list(ast.iter_child_nodes(node))))

def numpydoc_to_douki_yaml(raw: str) -> str:
    """
    title: Convert a NumPy-style docstring to Douki YAML format.
    parameters:
      raw: Original NumPy-style docstring text.
    returns: >-
      The YAML string (without triple-quotes). If *raw* is not a valid NumPy
      docstring, returns it unchanged.
    """
    if not _is_numpydoc_docstring(raw):
        return raw

    narrative, sections = _split_sections(raw)

    # Build Douki data structure
    data: dict[str, Any] = {}

    # Parse narrative into title + summary
    if narrative:
        nlines = narrative.splitlines()
        data['title'] = nlines[0].rstrip('.')
        if len(nlines) > 1:
            summary = '\n'.join(nlines[1:]).strip()
            if summary:
                data['summary'] = summary
    else:
        data['title'] = 'TODO'

    # Process sections
    for header, body in sections:
        douki_key = _NUMPY_SECTION_MAP.get(header)
        if douki_key is None:
            continue

        if douki_key in ('parameters', 'attributes'):
            data[douki_key] = {
                name: {'description': info.get('description', '')}
                for name, info in _parse_map_section(body).items()
            }
        elif douki_key in ('raises', 'warnings'):
            data[douki_key] = {
                name: info.get('description', '')
                for name, info in _parse_map_section(body).items()
            }
        elif douki_key in ('returns', 'yields', 'receives'):
            parsed = _parse_map_section(body)
            if parsed:
                description = ' '.join(
                    info['description'].strip()
                    for info in parsed.values()
                    if info.get('description')
                )
                data[douki_key] = (
                    description
                    if douki_key == 'returns'
                    else {'description': description}
                )
            else:
                # Simple text
                data[douki_key] = _parse_simple_section(body)
        else:
            data[douki_key] = _parse_simple_section(body)

    return format_documentation(data)

@typechecked
def check_source(source: str) -> None:
    """
    title: Validate annotations and authored documentation without changes.
    parameters:
      source: Python source code to validate.
    raises:
      DocstringValidationError: Missing or invalid documentation.
    """
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except SyntaxError as error:
        raise DocstringValidationError(f'syntax: {error.msg}') from error

    funcs = extract_functions(source)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and ast.get_docstring(node) is None:
            errors.append(f"- '{node.name}': missing docstring")
    for func in funcs:
        prefix = '<module>' if func.name == '<module>' else f"'{func.name}'"
        doc_node = func.docstring_node
        if doc_node is None:
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: missing docstring')
            continue
        if not isinstance(doc_node, ast.Constant):
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: invalid docstring node')
            continue
        try:
            raw = inspect.cleandoc(str(doc_node.value))
            data = normalize_documentation(_parse_validated_docstring(raw))
            validate_annotations(signature_for(func), data)
            errors.extend(
                f'- {prefix}: {problem}'
                for problem in completeness_errors(data, func)
            )
        except ValueError as error:
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: {error}')
    if errors:
        raise DocstringValidationError('\n'.join(errors))

def completeness_errors(data: dict[str, object], func: FuncInfo) -> list[str]:
    """
    title: Report missing, stale and placeholder descriptions.
    parameters:
      data: Schema-validated authored documentation.
      func: Parsed declaration metadata.
    returns: Documentation completeness diagnostics.
    """
    errors: list[str] = []
    if func.is_callable:
        documented = data.get('parameters', {})
        entries = documented if isinstance(documented, dict) else {}
        expected = {param.name for param in func.params}
        for stale in sorted(set(entries) - expected):
            errors.append(f"stale documented parameter '{stale}'")
        for name in sorted(expected):
            if not has_description(entries.get(name)):
                errors.append(f"missing description for parameter '{name}'")
        if needs_returns(func) and not has_description(data.get('returns')):
            errors.append('missing description for return value')

    documented_attrs = data.get('attributes', {})
    attr_entries = (
        documented_attrs if isinstance(documented_attrs, dict) else {}
    )
    for attr in func.attrs:
        if not has_description(attr_entries.get(attr.name)):
            errors.append(f"missing description for attribute '{attr.name}'")
    return errors

@private
@typechecked
def process_source(
    source: str,
    *,
    scaffold: bool,
    compact: bool = False,
    migrate: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    title: Format or scaffold documentation without storing types.
    parameters:
      source: Python source code.
      scaffold: Whether to scaffold missing documentation entries.
      compact: Whether to shorten description-only fields.
      migrate:
        optional: true
        description: Convert NumPy docstrings before processing when set.
    returns: The (possibly modified) source string.
    """
    # Optional migration pass first
    if migrate == 'numpydoc':
        source = _migrate_numpydoc(source)

    try:
        funcs = extract_functions(source)
    except SyntaxError:
        return source  # unparseable → leave alone

    if not funcs:
        return source

    # Check for missing docstrings — every function, class, and module
    # must have a docstring.
    missing = [f for f in funcs if f.docstring_node is None]
    if missing and scaffold:
        errors = []
        for f in missing:
            prefix = '<module>' if f.name == '<module>' else f"'{f.name}'"
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: missing docstring')
        raise DocstringValidationError('\n'.join(errors))

    lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    # Process in reverse line order so edits don't shift indices.
    funcs_with_ds = [f for f in funcs if f.docstring_node is not None]
    funcs_with_ds.sort(
        key=lambda f: f.docstring_node.lineno,  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        reverse=True,
    )

    errors = []

    for func in funcs_with_ds:
        ds_node = func.docstring_node
        assert ds_node is not None

        raw = str(ds_node.value)

        # Parse and validate once, then pass the mapping to the sync engine.
        try:
            parsed = _parse_validated_docstring(inspect.cleandoc(raw))
            if scaffold:
                validate_annotations(signature_for(func), parsed)
                scaffold_fields(parsed, func)
        except ValueError as e:
            prefix = (
                '<module>' if func.name == '<module>' else f"'{func.name}'"
            )
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: {e}')
            continue

        # We need the start/end lines of the docstring.
        ds_start = ds_node.lineno - 1  # 0-based
        ds_end = ds_node.end_lineno
        if ds_end is None or ds_node.end_col_offset is None:
            continue  # safety

        # AST columns are UTF-8 byte offsets. Retain adjacent comments/code.
        prefix = (
            lines[ds_start]
            .encode('utf-8')[: ds_node.col_offset]
            .decode('utf-8')
        )
        suffix = (
            lines[ds_end - 1]
            .encode('utf-8')[ds_node.end_col_offset :]
            .decode('utf-8')
        )

        # Extract the original docstring region
        original_region = ''.join(lines[ds_start:ds_end])

        # Detect quote style and indentation
        stripped_first = lines[ds_start].lstrip()
        indent = lines[ds_start][: len(lines[ds_start]) - len(stripped_first)]

        # Find the quote style
        quote_match = re.search(
            r'(\"\"\"|\'\'\')',
            original_region,
        )
        if not quote_match:
            continue  # pragma: no cover
        quote = quote_match.group(1)

        # Detect content indent from existing lines.
        content_indent = indent
        ds_lines = raw.split('\n')
        for dl in ds_lines[1:]:
            if dl.strip():
                leading = len(dl) - len(dl.lstrip())
                content_indent = ' ' * leading
                break

        try:
            formatted_data = (
                compact_documentation(parsed) if compact else parsed
            )
            if compact:
                formatted_data = style_description_blocks(
                    formatted_data,
                    width=79 - len(content_indent),
                )
            synced = format_documentation(
                formatted_data,
                width=79 - len(content_indent),
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            prefix = (
                '<module>' if func.name == '<module>' else f"'{func.name}'"
            )
            errors.append(f'- {prefix}: {e}')
            continue

        if synced == raw:
            continue

        # Rebuild the docstring with proper indentation
        synced_lines = synced.splitlines()
        formatted_lines = []
        for sl in synced_lines:
            if sl.strip():
                formatted_lines.append(content_indent + sl)
            else:
                formatted_lines.append('')
        new_content = '\n'.join(formatted_lines)
        new_content = new_content.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace(
            quote,
            '\\' + quote,
        )
        new_docstring = (
            f'{prefix}{quote}\n{new_content}\n{indent}{quote}{suffix}'
        )

        lines[ds_start:ds_end] = [new_docstring]

    if errors:
        errors.reverse()
        raise DocstringValidationError('\n'.join(errors))

    return ''.join(lines)

def scaffold_fields(data: dict[str, object], func: FuncInfo) -> None:
    """
    title: Add missing description placeholders without storing types.

        if raw_attrs is not None and not isinstance(raw_attrs, dict):
            raise ValueError('schema: attributes must be a mapping')
        existing_attrs = dict(raw_attrs) if raw_attrs is not None else {}
        for attr in func.attrs:
            existing_attrs.setdefault(attr.name, '...')
        data['attributes'] = existing_attrs
